notes: Experiment solid and bit-reproduced by all 4 reviewers. Key findings: PyTorch fp32 cliff 15.95-16.64 depending on wrong-class mass spread (fp16 7.63, bf16 5.54); autocast runs CE in fp32; Adam eps=1e-7 removed Slingshot spikes 5/5 like the fix; label smoothing 0.01 prevented grokking in 10k steps; loss on bf16 logits = 41 spikes/run; digits MLP puts 95-97% of train examples past the fp32 cliff harmlessly; custom autograd.Function fix costs 1.6-3.4x on CPU. Lessons: (1) never downsample time series that contain spikes - plot all points or bin by max; (2) when a column says 'reached X', also give 'at end'; (3) every takeaway sentence must be checked against every arm in our own table (label smoothing was contradicted in the takeaways after being reported correctly in results); (4) when replacing an inline <script> block by string search, the first '</script>' after a div may be the CDN tag - check for duplicate blocks; (5) pkill -f patterns self-match: kill by PID; (6) lr 1e-3 didn't grok on our 1-layer model within 10k steps - pilot the reproduction before launching the grid. Four reviews again found new precision issues each round: write the takeaway section last and run a scripted claim-vs-table check before review 1.
